title: MuSc: Zero-Shot Industrial Anomaly Classification and Segmentation with Mutual Scoring of the Unlabeled Images

en.text: Automated visual inspection on a factory line has to answer two questions about every product image at once: is there a defect (anomaly classification, AC), and where exactly is it, down to the pixel (anomaly segmentation, AS)? Two families of methods dominate. One-class methods build a memory bank of normal appearance, which means collecting a large set of defect-free reference images for every product. CLIP-based zero-shot methods skip the reference images but lean on hand-written text prompts instead.

Both assumptions get awkward in practice. Gathering normal samples is a poor fit for new products or short production runs, and writing good prompts is both an art and a losing battle against the sheer variety of real defects. The setting that actually matches a factory floor is stricter: no training, no prompts, and no normal reference images, yet still a pixel-level defect map and an image-level verdict.

MuSc (short for Mutual Scoring), presented at ICLR 2024, is built for exactly that setting. Its central observation is almost mundane: a batch of unlabeled test images already contains enough normal and abnormal evidence to find defects on its own. Normal appearance repeats across images, while defects are rare and idiosyncratic, so if you let the images score one another, the anomalies fall out with no labels required.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms compared. (a) A memory-bank one-class method needs many normal reference images; (b) a CLIP-based zero-shot method relies on extra text prompts; (c) MuSc uses only the unlabeled test images, scoring them at both the patch and image level.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16753  ·  Code: https://github.com/xrli-U/MuSc
Why mutual scoring works

The intuition rests on a checkable statistical regularity. Split a batch of same-product test images into patches. A normal patch tends to find many near-identical patches in the other images, because normal texture recurs. An abnormal patch finds only a handful of close matches, because a defect is rare and rarely repeats. That asymmetry, in how many similar neighbors a patch has, is by itself a training-free discriminative signal.
A three-stage pipeline

MuSc extracts features with a frozen vision transformer, ViT-L/14-336 from OpenAI's CLIP, never fine-tuned, and threads them through three modules: Local Neighborhood Aggregation with Multiple Degrees (LNAMD), the Mutual Scoring Mechanism (MSM), and Re-scoring with a Constrained Image-level Neighborhood (RsCIN). The figure below is easiest to read by following the data flow from left to right.

en.caption: Figure 2. The MuSc architecture. Patch tokens from a frozen ViT are aggregated by LNAMD at several degrees r to represent defects of different sizes; MSM lets the test images score each other to produce the segmentation map; RsCIN then refines the image-level score using the class tokens.

en.text: LNAMD comes first. It aggregates each patch token at several spatial scales, using degrees r ∈ {1, 3, 5}. Small r captures tiny defects, common on VisA, while large r captures the larger defects common on MVTec AD; combining all three covers a range of defect sizes rather than betting on one.
MSM: images scoring images

MSM is the heart of the method. Each patch's anomaly score is the distance to its nearest match in every other test image. A normal patch has close neighbors everywhere, so that distance stays small; an abnormal patch's stays large. But naively averaging over all images is fragile: an abnormal patch will occasionally land near a similar-looking region in some image, dragging its average down.
MuSc's fix is to keep, for each patch, only the smallest 30% of those mutual scores before averaging. The histograms below show why that helps.

en.caption: Figure 4. Top: raw nearest-neighbor distances for all normal (a) and abnormal (b) patches. Bottom: scores after averaging over the whole interval (c) versus only the minimum 30% interval (d); blue is normal, orange is abnormal. Restricting to the minimum interval visibly shrinks the overlap between the two.

en.text: Compare (c) and (d): averaging only the minimum 30% interval narrows the overlap (the brown region) between the normal and abnormal distributions, so a single threshold separates them far more cleanly. The ablations bear this out: on MVTec AD the "30% + mean" strategy reaches 97.8% image-level AUROC, against just 83.8% for a max-based strategy.
RsCIN: polishing the image-level call

The third stage, RsCIN, targets image-level classification specifically. It builds a constrained neighborhood graph over the class tokens with a multi-window mask, and calls an image normal only when it and its nearest neighbors all look normal, which suppresses the occasional misranked sample.

en.caption: Figure 5. Top: histograms of image-level anomaly scores before (a) and after (b) RsCIN, blue for normal and orange for abnormal. Bottom: a normal and an abnormal re-scoring example. After RsCIN the two classes separate more cleanly.

en.text: On VisA, RsCIN lifts image-level AUROC from 90.0% to 92.8%. It is also a plug-in: bolted onto other classification methods, it delivers a consistent boost there too.
Results: zero-shot, yet rivaling supervised methods

On the two standard industrial benchmarks, MVTec AD (15 categories, 10 objects plus 5 textures) and VisA (12 object categories), MuSc sets a new zero-shot state of the art. Classification is scored with AUROC, AP, and F1-max; segmentation adds pixel-level AUROC, F1-max, AP, and Per-Region Overlap (PRO).

en.caption: Figure 6. Anomaly-segmentation visualizations on MVTec AD (left) and VisA (right): from left to right, the input image, ground-truth mask, APRIL-GAN at 0-shot and 4-shot, and MuSc at 0-shot. MuSc's heatmaps cover the true defect regions far more completely.

en.text: In numbers, MuSc reaches 97.8% image-level AUROC and 97.3% pixel-level AUROC on MVTec AD. On segmentation it beats the second-best zero-shot method by +21.1% PRO, +21.9% AP, and +18.4% F1-max. On VisA it gains more than ten points over the runner-up in both classification and segmentation.

en.caption: Table 1. Zero-shot comparison on MVTec AD and VisA (%). AUROC-cls is image-level classification, AUROC-segm is pixel-level segmentation, PRO is Per-Region Overlap.

en.text: The cross-setting comparison is the striking part. Using no reference images at all, MuSc outperforms most 4-shot methods, beats the 32-shot RegAD, matches the 8-shot GraphCore, and even holds its own against full-shot methods like CutPaste, IGD, and NSA that train on the entire normal set.
Takeaway and limits

MuSc's contribution is to make good use of a fact prior work left on the table: a batch of unlabeled test images can supervise itself. Because normal structure recurs across images while defects stand alone, mutual scoring pulls them apart, and zero-shot performance climbs to near-supervised levels for both classification and segmentation.

The approach does come with conditions. MuSc needs a batch of same-category test images to run, since a single isolated image has nothing to score against, and the all-pairs comparison carries an inference cost. The paper offers a knob that splits the dataset into s parts to cut per-image latency and memory (splitting into three parts drops per-image time from roughly 999 ms to about 514 ms). Where batched test data is available, MuSc is a practical starting point that asks for no training, no prompts, and no normal samples.

More broadly, MuSc is a reminder that the data you already have can carry more supervision than it first appears. Before reaching for labels, prompts, or a curated reference set, it can be worth asking whether the test batch itself already holds the answer, and simply needs a way to let its images compare notes.

zh.text: 在工业质检里，自动化的异常检测要同时回答两个问题：这张产品图有没有缺陷（分类，Anomaly Classification, AC），以及缺陷具体落在像素级的什么位置（分割，Anomaly Segmentation, AS）。过去的主流做法有两类：一类是基于记忆库（memory bank）的单类方法，需要为每种产品预先收集大量正常参考图；另一类是基于 CLIP 的零样本方法，需要人工设计文本提示（text prompt）。
这两条路都有现实门槛。收集正常样本对新产品、小批量生产并不友好；而手写提示既依赖经验，又很难覆盖形态各异的真实缺陷。真正贴近工厂落地的设定其实更苛刻：没有训练、没有提示、也没有任何正常参考图，却仍要在图像级判定异常、在像素级定位缺陷。
本文（ICLR 2024）提出的 MuSc（Mutual Scoring，互相打分）正是针对这一设定。它的核心观察很朴素：一批无标注的测试图像本身就藏着足够的“正常”与“异常”线索。正常区域的外观会在其他图像里反复出现，而缺陷罕见且各不相同，只要让这些图像互相打分，就能把异常从正常中区分出来，全程不需要任何标签。

zh.caption: 图1 三种范式对比：(a) 基于记忆库的单类方法需要大量正常参考图；(b) 基于 CLIP 的零样本方法依赖额外的文本提示；(c) MuSc 只利用无标注测试图像，在 patch 级与图像级同时完成分割与分类。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16753　｜　开源代码：https://github.com/xrli-U/MuSc
为什么“互相打分”能行
MuSc 的出发点是一个可验证的统计规律：把同一产品的一批测试图切成小块（patch），一个正常 patch 往往能在其他图像里找到很多相似 patch，因为正常外观是重复的；而一个异常 patch 只能找到极少数相似的，因为缺陷稀少且形态各异。这种“相似邻居数量”的不对称，本身就是一个无需训练的判别信号。
MuSc 的三步流水线
MuSc 用一个冻结的视觉 Transformer（ViT-L/14-336，来自 OpenAI CLIP，全程不做微调）提取特征，再串起三个模块：多度局部邻域聚合（LNAMD）、互相打分机制（MSM）与图像级约束邻域重打分（RsCIN）。看图时可以从左到右、跟着数据流走一遍。

zh.caption: 图2 MuSc 架构。冻结 ViT 提取的 patch token 经 LNAMD 在多个聚合度 r 下表示不同尺寸的缺陷，MSM 让测试图像互相打分得到分割结果，RsCIN 再利用图像级 class token 优化分类分数。

zh.text: 第一步 LNAMD（Local Neighborhood Aggregation with Multiple Degrees）把 patch token 在多个空间尺度上聚合。论文取聚合度 r∈{1,3,5}：小的 r 关注细小缺陷（在 VisA 上常见），大的 r 关注大面积缺陷（在 MVTec AD 上常见），三者结合覆盖不同缺陷尺寸。
MSM：让图像互相打分
第二步 MSM（Mutual Scoring Mechanism）是方法的核心。每个 patch 的异常分，取它在“其他每一张测试图”里最近邻的距离；正常 patch 因为处处有相似邻居，最近邻距离很小，异常 patch 则偏大。但直接对所有图像的分数求平均并不稳妥，因为异常 patch 偶尔也会在个别图里撞上相似区域，把平均值拉低。
MuSc 的做法是：对每个 patch，只保留所有互相打分里最小的 30% 区间再取平均。下面这组直方图解释了为什么这样更好。

zh.caption: 图4 上排：所有正常 patch (a) 与异常 patch (b) 的原始最近邻距离分布。下排：对全区间取平均 (c) 与只对最小 30% 区间取平均 (d) 后的分数分布，蓝色为正常、橙色为异常。只取最小区间后，正常与异常的重叠明显减小。

zh.text: 对比 (c) 与 (d)：只保留最小 30% 区间求平均，正常与异常分布的重叠（棕色部分）明显收窄，两类更容易被一个阈值分开。消融实验也印证了这一点——在 MVTec AD 上，“30% + 取平均”策略把图像级 AUROC 做到 97.8%，而换成取最大值的策略只有 83.8%。
RsCIN：把图像级判断再擦亮一遍
第三步 RsCIN（Re-scoring with Constrained Image-level Neighborhood）专门优化图像级分类。它在 class token 上构建一个受约束的邻域图，并配合多窗口掩码：只有当一张图和它的近邻都“看起来正常”时，才把它判为正常，从而抑制个别被误判的样本。

zh.caption: 图5 上排：使用 RsCIN 前 (a) 与后 (b) 的图像级异常分数直方图，蓝色为正常、橙色为异常。下排：一个正常与一个异常样本的重打分示例。RsCIN 之后正常与异常的分数更易区分。

zh.text: 在 VisA 上，RsCIN 把图像级 AUROC 从 90.0% 提升到 92.8%。值得一提的是，RsCIN 是即插即用的：把它接到别的分类方法上，同样能带来稳定的提升。
效果：零样本，却逼近甚至超过有标注方法
在两个标准工业基准 MVTec AD（15 类，10 个物体 + 5 种纹理）和 VisA（12 类物体）上，MuSc 都刷新了零样本的最好成绩。分类用 AUROC、AP、F1-max 衡量，分割额外用像素级 AUROC、F1-max、AP 与区域重叠度 PRO。

zh.caption: 图6 MVTec AD（左）与 VisA（右）上的异常分割可视化对比：从左到右依次为输入图、真值掩码、APRIL-GAN 的 0-shot 与 4-shot 结果，以及 MuSc 的 0-shot 结果。MuSc 的热力图更完整地覆盖了真实缺陷区域。

zh.text: 数字上，MuSc 在 MVTec AD 上达到 97.8% 图像级 AUROC 与 97.3% 像素级 AUROC；在分割指标上，比第二好的零样本方法高出 +21.1% PRO、+21.9% AP、+18.4% F1-max。在 VisA 上，分类与分割相比第二名都提升超过 10 个百分点。

zh.caption: 表1 MVTec AD 与 VisA 上零样本方法对比（%）。AUROC-cls 为图像级分类，AUROC-segm 为像素级分割，PRO 为区域重叠度。

zh.text: 更有意思的是横向对比：不用任何参考图的 MuSc，超过了大多数 4-shot 方法，胜过用 32 张样本的 RegAD，与 8-shot 的 GraphCore 相当，甚至可以和用上全部正常训练集的 full-shot 方法（如 CutPaste、IGD、NSA）掰手腕。
小结与边界
MuSc 的价值在于把一个被忽略的事实用好了：一批无标注测试图像可以充当自己的监督信号——正常结构在图像间反复出现、缺陷各自孤立，互相打分就能把两者分开，于是零样本也能逼近全监督的分类与分割效果。
当然，这套方法也有前提：MuSc 需要一批同类产品的测试图一起推理（batch），单张孤立图像无法互相打分；逐图两两比较也带来推理开销——论文把数据集分成 s 份来降低单图耗时与显存（分成 3 份可把单图耗时从约 999ms 降到约 514ms）。在具备成批测试数据的场景里，MuSc 是一个无需训练、无需提示、也无需正常样本的实用起点。

Gathering normal samples is a poor fit for new products or short production runs, and writing good prompts is both an art and a losing battle against the sheer variety of real defects. The setting that actually matches a factory floor is stricter: no training, no prompts, and no normal reference images, yet still a pixel-level defect map and an image-level verdict.

MuSc (short for Mutual Scoring), presented at ICLR 2024, is built for exactly that setting. Its central observation is almost mundane: a batch of unlabeled test images already contains enough normal and abnormal evidence to find defects on its own. Normal appearance repeats across images, while defects are rare and idiosyncratic, so if you let the images score one another, the anomalies fall out with no labels required.

en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms compared. (a) A memory-bank one-class method needs many normal reference images; (b) a CLIP-based zero-shot method relies on extra text prompts; (c) MuSc uses only the unlabeled test images, scoring them at both the patch and image level.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16753  ·  Code: https://github.com/xrli-U/MuSc
MSM: images scoring images

MSM is the heart of the method. Each patch's anomaly score is the distance to its nearest match in every other test image. A normal patch has close neighbors everywhere, so that distance stays small; an abnormal patch's stays large. But naively averaging over all images is fragile: an abnormal patch will occasionally land near a similar-looking region in some image, dragging its average down.
MuSc's fix is to keep, for each patch, only the smallest 30% of those mutual scores before averaging. The histograms below show why that helps.

en.caption: Figure 4. Top: raw nearest-neighbor distances for all normal (a) and abnormal (b) patches. Bottom: scores after averaging over the whole interval (c) versus only the minimum 30% interval (d); blue is normal, orange is abnormal. Restricting to the minimum interval visibly shrinks the overlap between the two.

en.text: Compare (c) and (d): averaging only the minimum 30% interval narrows the overlap (the brown region) between the normal and abnormal distributions, so a single threshold separates them far more cleanly. The ablations bear this out: on MVTec AD the "30% + mean" strategy reaches 97.8% image-level AUROC, against just 83.8% for a max-based strategy.

zh.text: 在工业质检里，自动化的异常检测要同时回答两个问题：这张产品图有没有缺陷（分类，Anomaly Classification, AC），以及缺陷具体落在像素级的什么位置（分割，Anomaly Segmentation, AS）。过去的主流做法有两类：一类是基于记忆库（memory bank）的单类方法，需要为每种产品预先收集大量正常参考图；另一类是基于 CLIP 的零样本方法，需要人工设计文本提示（text prompt）。
这两条路都有现实门槛。收集正常样本对新产品、小批量生产并不友好；而手写提示既依赖经验，又很难覆盖形态各异的真实缺陷。真正贴近工厂落地的设定其实更苛刻：没有训练、没有提示、也没有任何正常参考图，却仍要在图像级判定异常、在像素级定位缺陷。
本文（ICLR 2024）提出的 MuSc（Mutual Scoring，互相打分）正是针对这一设定。它的核心观察很朴素：一批无标注的测试图像本身就藏着足够的“正常”与“异常”线索。正常区域的外观会在其他图像里反复出现，而缺陷罕见且各不相同，只要让这些图像互相打分，就能把异常从正常中区分出来，全程不需要任何标签。

zh.caption: 图1 三种范式对比：(a) 基于记忆库的单类方法需要大量正常参考图；(b) 基于 CLIP 的零样本方法依赖额外的文本提示；(c) MuSc 只利用无标注测试图像，在 patch 级与图像级同时完成分割与分类。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16753　｜　开源代码：https://github.com/xrli-U/MuSc
MSM：让图像互相打分
第二步 MSM（Mutual Scoring Mechanism）是方法的核心。每个 patch 的异常分，取它在“其他每一张测试图”里最近邻的距离；正常 patch 因为处处有相似邻居，最近邻距离很小，异常 patch 则偏大。但直接对所有图像的分数求平均并不稳妥，因为异常 patch 偶尔也会在个别图里撞上相似区域，把平均值拉低。

zh.caption: 图4 上排：所有正常 patch (a) 与异常 patch (b) 的原始最近邻距离分布。下排：对全区间取平均 (c) 与只对最小 30% 区间取平均 (d) 后的分数分布，蓝色为正常、橙色为异常。只取最小区间后，正常与异常的重叠明显减小。

zh.text: 对比 (c) 与 (d)：只保留最小 30% 区间求平均，正常与异常分布的重叠（棕色部分）明显收窄，两类更容易被一个阈值分开。消融实验也印证了这一点——在 MVTec AD 上，“30% + 取平均”策略把图像级 AUROC 做到 97.8%，而换成取最大值的策略只有 83.8%。

en.text: Automated visual inspection on a factory line has to answer two questions about every product image at once: is there a defect (anomaly classification, AC), and where exactly is it, down to the pixel (anomaly segmentation, AS)? Two families of methods dominate. One-class methods build a memory bank of normal appearance, which means collecting a large set of defect-free reference images for every product. CLIP-based zero-shot methods skip the reference images but lean on hand-written text prompts instead.

Both assumptions get awkward in practice. Gathering normal samples is a poor fit for new products or short production runs, and writing good prompts is both an art and a losing battle against the sheer variety of real defects. The setting that actually matches a factory floor is stricter: no training, no prompts, and no normal reference images, yet still a pixel-level defect map and an image-level verdict.

MuSc (short for Mutual Scoring), presented at ICLR 2024, is built for exactly that setting. en.caption: Figure 1. Three paradigms compared. (a) A memory-bank one-class method needs many normal reference images; (b) a CLIP-based zero-shot method relies on extra text prompts; (c) MuSc uses only the unlabeled test images, scoring them at both the patch and image level.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.16753  ·  Code: https://github.com/xrli-U/MuSc
Takeaway and limits

MuSc's contribution is to make good use of a fact prior work left on the table: a batch of unlabeled test images can supervise itself. Because normal structure recurs across images while defects stand alone, mutual scoring pulls them apart, and zero-shot performance climbs to near-supervised levels for both classification and segmentation.

The approach does come with conditions. MuSc needs a batch of same-category test images to run, since a single isolated image has nothing to score against, and the all-pairs comparison carries an inference cost. The paper offers a knob that splits the dataset into s parts to cut per-image latency and memory (splitting into three parts drops per-image time from roughly 999 ms to about 514 ms). Where batched test data is available, MuSc is a practical starting point that asks for no training, no prompts, and no normal samples.

More broadly, MuSc is a reminder that the data you already have can carry more supervision than it first appears. Before reaching for labels, prompts, or a curated reference set, it can be worth asking whether the test batch itself already holds the answer, and simply needs a way to let its images compare notes.

zh.caption: 图1 三种范式对比：(a) 基于记忆库的单类方法需要大量正常参考图；(b) 基于 CLIP 的零样本方法依赖额外的文本提示；(c) MuSc 只利用无标注测试图像，在 patch 级与图像级同时完成分割与分类。

zh.text: 小结与边界
MuSc 的价值在于把一个被忽略的事实用好了：一批无标注测试图像可以充当自己的监督信号——正常结构在图像间反复出现、缺陷各自孤立，互相打分就能把两者分开，于是零样本也能逼近全监督的分类与分割效果。
当然，这套方法也有前提：MuSc 需要一批同类产品的测试图一起推理（batch），单张孤立图像无法互相打分；逐图两两比较也带来推理开销——论文把数据集分成 s 份来降低单图耗时与显存（分成 3 份可把单图耗时从约 999ms 降到约 514ms）。在具备成批测试数据的场景里，MuSc 是一个无需训练、无需提示、也无需正常样本的实用起点。
